newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends lower, intermonth spreads ease more.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends lower, intermonth spreads ease more.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures ended sharply lower on Monday in a continuation of a two-month downtrend as U.S. refined products tumbled and NYMEX crude oil futures broke lower beneath key technical support, traders said.
April IPE Brent closed 66 cents a barrel down at $19.13 a barrel while NYMEX crude oil was 67 cents off at $20.72.
"It is weaker U.S. products and the WTI (NYMEX futures) breaking support, very much so," one IPE dealer said.

Dealers said while weakness in U.S. refined oil products futures was the motor behind Monday's downwards move, the bears were given an extra boost when April NYMEX crude fell through strong psycholigical support at $21.00 a barrel, the first time since August last year.
"It does look poor, very poor," another IPE dealer said.
March NYMEX heating oil had shed 2.20 cents a gallon at the close and stood at 55.65 cents. March NYMEX gasoline, too, was 1.52 cents weaker at 60.30.

Independent forecasters Weather Services Corp. (WSC) said that while temperatures in the key heating oil markets of the northeastern United States would be well below normal on Tuesday, this would change towards the end of the week and temperatures were expected to become above normal by then.
Temperatures in Europe over the week would be above normal, WSC added.

The spread between April and May Brent slipped six cents on the day to 19 cents and dealers suggest the long-backwardated market may soon move into contango. The spread between the front and second months was around 90 cents last October.
Contango on crude oil "looks possible, perhaps even probable," said Nigel Saperia, managing director of the oil division at Bankers' Trust International.
Swaps markets for refined oil products in Europe have now moved into a light contango in some cases.
